- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

+/* Sideways slides simulate physical movement across the viewport, the most
+   common trigger for motion sensitivity. Zeroing the durations drops every

aiTitle: Add view transitions to product gallery

content.text:
All four patterns are in, verified against the view-transitions guide that ships with this exact Next version (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/view-transitions.md`). `tsc --noEmit`, `next build`, and `next dev` all pass clean; both routes render the expected `vt-*` markers and `transitionTypes` reaches the client payload.

## What changed

**`app/view-transitions.ts`** (new) — the `<ViewTransition>` configs in one place, so the grid and the detail page can't drift apart on the shared `name`:

- `productImage(slug)` → `name: product-${slug}`, `share: 'morph'`, `default: 'none'`
- `pageSlide` → `enter`/`exit` maps keyed by transition type
- `skeletonReveal` / `contentReveal` → the Suspense handoff

**Shared element morph** — the grid thumbnail (`app/ProductGrid.tsx`) and the detail hero (`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`) are wrapped in `<ViewTransition>` with the same name, so React pairs them and animates size/position between the two. A 400ms group duration with a mid-flight blur keyframe hides interpolation artifacts between the 4:3 thumbnail and the 1:1 hero.

**Directional slides** — card links carry `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`, the back link `['nav-back']`. Each `page.tsx` root is wrapped in `pageSlide`, which maps those types to ±60px slides (in the page, not the layout — layouts persist, so enter/exit never fire there). Untyped transitions resolve to `none`, so browser back/forward and Suspense reveals don't slide sideways.

**Suspense reveals** — both boundaries (grid and detail info) now have the fallback exiting `slide-down` and the content entering `slide-up`, with asymmetric timing: exit 150ms, enter fade 210ms delayed behind it, slide 400ms.

One deliberate departure from the guide: I scoped the reveal classes to untyped transitions (`{'nav-forward': 'none', 'nav-back': 'none', default: 'slide-up'}`) rather than applying them unconditionally. `ProductGrid` never suspends, so on `nav-back` its content is always present in the navigation commit — with an unconditional `enter="slide-up"` the grid would break out of the page group and slide *up* while the surrounding page slid *right*. Scoped this way, it travels with the page during navigation and only slides on the actual skeleton→content handoff.

**Reduced motion** — `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroes `animation-duration`/`animation-delay` on `::view-transition-group/image-pair/old/new(*)`, dropping everything back to the browser's instant swap; navigation, morph, and reveals still function. I also stopped the skeletons' looping `pulse` there, since that's motion too.

Two small extras: `::view-transition { pointer-events: none }` so clicks during an animation aren't swallowed by the overlay, and an explicit `border-radius` on `.product-image` — it was relying on the card's `overflow: hidden`, which stops applying once the thumbnail is lifted into the transition overlay, so its corners would have flashed square mid-morph.

**`react-canary.d.ts`** (new) — `<ViewTransition>`'s types live in `@types/react`'s `canary` entry point and need one triple-slash reference. I used a reference file rather than `compilerOptions.types`, which would have suppressed the automatic `@types/node` include.

## Notes

- Running `next dev` generated `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in the repo root. Those aren't mine — Next writes them itself (`next dev` re-adds the block on every run), so I left them rather than deleting something that would immediately come back.
- Unrelated pre-existing issue I did not touch: the detail page returns a bare `<div>`, not `<main>`, so it misses the `max-width: 1200px` and `2rem` padding the home page gets. The hero therefore renders full-bleed and much larger than the layout implies, which the morph now makes more noticeable. Wrapping it in `<main>` would fix it, but that's a visible layout change you didn't ask for — say the word and I'll do it.
- I couldn't verify the animations visually: there's no browser binary in this sandbox. The checks above confirm the markup, props, and build are correct, but the actual motion is unverified.
